content:
Apple has filed for a preliminary injunction in its ongoing trade secrets lawsuit against OpenAI. Apple stated that without a preliminary injunction, it would suffer "irreparable harm" due to the theft of trade secrets.

In the filing, Apple explained that after filing its first lawsuit last month, it wrote to OpenAI expressing its "intent to move for preliminary injunctive relief." However, Apple noted that if OpenAI agreed to the following five requests, this step could be avoided:

  • Cease accessing or using Apple's confidential information
  • Immediately stop any related use or disclosure
  • Preserve all evidence
  • Allow forensic examination of devices, cloud storage, email, Slack, Teams, and other repositories
  • Search OpenAI's systems for any Apple confidential information

Apple stated that OpenAI has agreed to the first three requests, but the two parties have not reached a consensus on the final two.

Therefore, Apple is asking the court to issue a preliminary injunction requiring the judge to immediately bar OpenAI from using or obtaining any Apple trade secrets, preserve all evidence, allow Apple to conduct forensic examinations of OpenAI's devices and accounts, and retrieve any Apple confidential information still in OpenAI's possession.

Apple said:

Apple has also separately filed a motion asking the court to accelerate discovery procedures, including early document production and out-of-court depositions of OpenAI's key employees and management.

Coinciding with Apple's filing, OpenAI also issued its most extensive public response to the lawsuit to date. In a late-night blog post, OpenAI noted that this "rushed, aggressive, and unusually personal" lawsuit is inconsistent with Apple's longstanding reputation as "one of the greatest companies in history."

The injunction hearing is scheduled for October 1, 2026. The full filing can be viewed below.
